title: MCP = Mega Context Problem - Matt Carey
talk_summary: Matt Carey argues MCP's main failure mode is dumping huge tool/API schemas into context, and compares progressive discovery via CLI, tool search, and code mode. He then advocates sandboxed code execution with guardrails, saved generated scripts, and stateless cloud-native agent loops.

takeaways.technique: Progressive tool discovery instead of full tool schemas
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a small search/help surface and load only relevant tool definitions into context per task, rather than injecting every API endpoint or tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We just shouldn't be dumping loads of tools into context.
takeaways.numbers: OpenAPI 2.3M tokens; tools ~1.1M tokens; 2,600 endpoints; 16 MCP servers; tool search K=8 ~2,100 tokens with ~500 used.

takeaways.technique: Code mode against generated typed SDK
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate a typed SDK from OpenAPI and give the model one code-execution tool; the model writes code against types instead of making many individual tool calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one tool called code where the model generates the code of your choice and then you run it

takeaways.technique: Programmable sandbox guardrails for generated code
takeaways.what_they_do: Run generated code in isolated V8/Deno/Python sandboxes with secrets absent by default and network/domain access toggled by policy.
Persist successful generated code as mini scripts or cron jobs; when a brittle script breaks, the agent repairs and resaves it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent will fix it and resave the script

takeaways.technique: Stateless agent loop with externalized state
takeaways.what_they_do: Design agents as cloud-native stateless loops where state can be turned on or off, instead of keeping one long-lived sandbox per agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: state has to be something you can turn on or off

takeaways.what_they_do: Assume agents will hammer APIs in loops from multiple sandboxes, so add strong rate limiting and protection at the API boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your APIs have to be ready to take a beating
